key_insight: Video Streaming Thinking (VST) enables VideoLLMs to 'think while watching' by running a synchronized reasoning stream alongside a fast perception stream, reducing response latency while preserving coherent logical inference.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between low-latency streaming perception and synchronized, high-quality reasoning in online VideoLLMs, avoiding the unacceptable delay caused by naive test-time scaling.
method: Dual-stream architecture: a fast perception stream ingests video frames continuously while a parallel reasoning (thinking) stream processes accumulated context at a controllable cadence.
Asynchronous, event-driven scheduling: selectively activate reasoning steps (or scale compute) based on perceptual cues, reducing unnecessary computation and end-to-end delay.

Incremental context fusion and memory compression: continuously align and summarize incoming visual information so the reasoning stream accesses up-to-date, compact context without waiting for full-frame batches.
impact: Enables real-time, interactive VideoLLMs that provide low-latency responses with sustained logical coherence—important for applications like live video assistant, robotics, and surveillance where both speed and reasoning matter.
